theme: GLA Site Allocations semantics, provenance and licence
formula: 20 source facts x 4 assertion roles x 10 control families x 25 validation stages = 20000 rows

facts.fact: A Site Allocation identifies a site for a particular development or use within a development plan.
The dataset describes potential uses including housing, employment and leisure.
Allocated sites provide guidelines for planning decisions.
The GIS boundaries are described as indicative.
Users are instructed to contact the relevant London Borough to confirm accuracy.
The dataset is published under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
The dataset includes a GeoPackage resource.
The Site Allocations GeoPackage is approximately 5.11 MB.
The GeoPackage projection is EPSG:27700 British National Grid.
The dataset page lists three resources.
The web mapping service points to planning_data_map_02 MapServer layer 102.
The smallest geography is custom polygons.
GLA data is useful for screening but borough confirmation is explicitly required.
An indicative GLA boundary is not automatically a borough-confirmed positive binding.
A complete GLA layer exclusion may support a GLA-layer negative only.
A GLA-layer result must remain separate from borough target-layer evidence.
A 403 resource link is a transport condition, not a spatial result.
GeoPackage availability does not prove a candidate intersection.
The current exact GLA Site Allocations negative count remains one.
No new GLA exact relation is added without executable geometry or query evidence.
